content: Additional imaging studies are frequently conducted to assess potential damage to target organs in patients diagnosed with hypertension. An electrocardiogram (EKG/ECG) is utilized to determine whether left ventricular hypertrophy is present or to detect evidence of a silent myocardial infarction. A chest X-ray is performed to identify any indications of cardiac enlargement or signs suggestive of heart failure. An echocardiogram is employed to confirm the presence of left ventricular hypertrophy and to evaluate for diastolic dysfunction.
